language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hello! I hope you are having a nice journey on Flight Matters. You have been chosen for a special tour of 'Matters'.

If you were looking out of our window you would have seen that we have passed the snowy mountains, flying over the Atlantic Ocean: over the Bermuda Triangle. And shortly, we will be flying through many clouds.

Did you see that this covers our three states of matter? I'll explain:
Solid: snow is solid water.
Liquid: the ocean is liquid water.
Gas: clouds are water in gas form.
It is all water, but each time in a different state.
Our special feature today is to find out what happens when matter is heated or cooled. Let’s look at this together.
Hello, I am Tim.
Hello! I hope you are having a nice journey on Flight Matters. You have been chosen for a special tour of 'Matters'.

If you were looking out of our window you would have seen that we have passed the snowy mountains, flying over the Atlantic Ocean: over the Bermuda Triangle. And shortly, we will be flying through many clouds.

Did you see that this covers our three states of matter? I'll explain:
Solid: snow is solid water.
Liquid: the ocean is liquid water.
Gas: clouds are water in gas form.
It is all water, but each time in a different state.
Our special feature today is to find out what happens when matter is heated or cooled. Let’s look at this together.

You know that in solids the particles are packed tightly together. When heat is applied, the particles move apart, and when hot enough a solid becomes a liquid. So in liquids the particles are further apart. In gases, the particles are even further apart. Knowing this, can you sort the following pictures?

Hi! Welcome to the galley. I’ve just put a kettle on. That reminds me, you already know that when an object is heated, the particles move away from each other.
But, did you know this also makes an object expand? And when you cool an object the particles move closer: this makes the object contract.
When the Concorde used to fly it would become so warm that the plane could expand up to 20 centimeters! Here are some examples of expansion and contraction in our daily life.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: To fit a metal rim onto a wooden wheel, the rim is heated so it expands. It is then slipped over the woodel wheel. After cooling the rim __________ and fits tightly over the wheel.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: Concreet roads have spaces between each block so that the conrete can __________ in hot climates.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: When the air is heated it __________. This causes the balloon to rise.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: In winter the mercury in a thermometer would contract, and the level would __________.

outro.text: Fantastic! Keep looking out for other forms of expansion and contraction everywhere.
